events.title: Battle of the Aegates Islands
events.description: Off the western coast of Sicily, a Roman fleet destroyed a Carthaginian fleet that was carrying supplies to Sicily. The victory ended the First Punic War.
events.significance: Rome's victory ended Carthage's challenge for control of the western Mediterranean. It set Rome on the path to becoming the dominant Mediterranean power.

events.title: Charles I Dissolves Parliament
events.description: King Charles I of England dissolved Parliament. He then ruled for eleven years without calling another one, a period known as the Personal Rule or the 'Eleven Years' Tyranny'.
events.significance: The standoff between king and Parliament deepened, and it helped lead to the English Civil War.

events.title: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo Ratified
events.description: The U.S. Senate ratified the treaty that ended the Mexican-American War. Mexico ceded a vast territory that included present-day California, Nevada, Utah and much of the Southwest.
events.significance: The treaty reshaped the map of North America and greatly expanded the United States.

events.title: The First Telephone Call
events.description: In Boston, Alexander Graham Bell spoke to his assistant Thomas Watson in another room and said, 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.' It is regarded as the first successful telephone call.
events.significance: The call demonstrated that speech could be carried over wires. That led to a global telephone network and changed how people communicate.

events.title: Death of Harriet Tubman
events.description: Harriet Tubman, who escaped slavery and became a conductor on the Underground Railroad, died in Auburn, New York. She later served the Union Army and worked for women's suffrage.
events.significance: Tubman is remembered as a symbol of courage and freedom. Harriet Tubman Day is observed in parts of the United States on March 10.
